records.note: Court and law-enforcement resourcing, deterrence and the speed of resolution for victims: not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. Also conditional on court funding with no observable event, and 'might shrink enough' has no benchmark.

Court delays for people who file complaints against predators: outside the five areas. Also a standing generalization ('doomed to wait years') with no dated call, no countable set and no named source.

'Medical devices that modulate the brain will be the future' is a slogan: no entity, event, series, benchmark, threshold or countable set. 'The future' is not a deadline. Practice-adoption area guess, but nothing can be written without inventing a series and a threshold.

A generalizability judgment about the EMPOWER home tDCS trial (Flow Neuroscience). No trial, sample, endpoint or threshold is named for a Medicaid population, so no event can be written without inventing one.

Comparative without a benchmark: 'SAINT-level efficacy' is not quantified in the forecaster's words (he gives tDCS effect sizes 0.46 and 0.37 but no SAINT figure), and no trial or endpoint is named. 'Shouldn't expect' reads as predictive (do not expect, bin D), but no event can be written with nothing invented.
The 2024 US presidential election result in New York: outside the five areas. Also near-known (New York is not a swing state) and 'do very little' has no threshold.

The newsletter's own future editorial stances: the forecaster's own organization (The Frontier Psychiatrists) decides. Also outside the five areas. Satirical post, but the sentence reads sincere; CONTROL is the primary failing test.

'That will take technology and better contracts' names no entity, event, series or threshold; 'the future' is not a deadline. Structural claim about what improvement requires, not a resolvable forecast.

Trial start by the forecaster's own organizations: Psyrin (strategic advisor) sponsors, Fermata (co-founder, Brooklyn) and Acacia Clinics (clinician and trial site, Sunnyvale) enroll. Own-venture commitment, never scored. 'Soon' is not a deadline in any case.

Announcement of a rollout by 'our partners' at Living Water Clinics, a partner of the forecaster's own organization Fermata (co-founder), listed among the author's own developments in the same section. A joint rollout inside the author's network is an own-venture commitment; the present-progressive wording ('are also bringing') also passes on information rather than an expectation. Living Water Clinics is not in the affiliation list, so a coder who reads it as an independent third party would code REPORT (announcement, no expectation). No confidence phrase and no time words.

General claim that whole-body screening (Prenuvo) will produce enough false positives to cause harm from follow-up workups: no series, threshold, population or period; 'wrong enough' has no benchmark. The 'terrible idea' framing is normative.
Systematic error (herding) in 2024 US presidential election polls: outside the five areas.
The 2024 US presidential election outcome ('could go either way'): outside the five areas.
Restates the poll-error call of owen-1302 in the same post; election polling accuracy is outside the five areas. Not DUPLICATE: a different sentence, not the same extraction captured twice.
False post-election claims by a candidate and the effect of turnout on them: outside the five areas; also hedged ('could') with no observable threshold.

'More' side effects discovered at large scale: a quantifier with no countable set, threshold or named resolution source. The forecaster does not say how discovery is recorded (a label revision, a safety communication, adverse-event reports), so writing a Cobenfy label-change event would invent the resolution mechanism. A coder who reads 'discover more' as an FDA label revision adding an adverse reaction would propose such an event; this coder does not.

event.title: FDA approves xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for bipolar disorder
event.proposition: The FDA approves xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for a bipolar disorder indication.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date the FDA approval letter or the Drugs@FDA entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) is dated for an application that adds a bipolar disorder indication to the xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) label. Any bipolar I or bipolar II indication counts (for example, acute manic or mixed episodes, depressive episodes, or maintenance), as monotherapy or as an adjunct, and the reading is logged. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote, a filing acceptance, a trial start or a trial result is not an approval. Approval by a regulator other than the FDA does not count.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (xanomeline-trospium / Cobenfy approval letters and labeling); Bristol Myers Squibb press release as a secondary source

readings: 'They are going to be bringing this drug to bipolar disorder' is read as FDA approval of xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for a bipolar disorder indication: the observable end state of bringing a drug to a condition. A trial start, a trial result or a filing does not resolve the event.
'bipolar disorder' includes any bipolar I or bipolar II indication, as monotherapy or adjunct; a label narrower than 'bipolar disorder' counts, per the drug_approval template rule.
'and other conditions' is split off as owen-1309-b and is not written into this event.

records.phrase: They are going to be bringing this drug to bipolar disorder
records.stage_note: At the statement date, per the post, Cobenfy (xanomeline-trospium) was newly FDA-approved for schizophrenia (September 2024). For bipolar disorder the forecaster names no trial, phase, filing or PDUFA date, and the coder assigns no program stage from outside the statement. No base-rate class fits an indication expansion with no stated stage, so b is null.
records.note: First half of an 'A and B' claim (bipolar disorder; other conditions). Third party decides (the FDA on a Bristol Myers Squibb application); the author spells the sponsor 'Bristol Meyers Squibb'. Bin A on 'are going to be' (lexicon A phrase 'is going to'), asserts true. 'Not done yet' and the claim sentence carry no time words, so deadline null and the item goes to the undated panel (24-month window from 2024-11-13). Not REPORT: no source is cited and no dated internal action is named. Not KNOWN: no FDA approval for bipolar disorder existed on the statement date. Not affiliated: Bristol Myers Squibb and the FDA are not in the forecaster's affiliation list.

Second half of an 'A and B' claim: 'and other conditions' is an unnamed set of indications with no countable set, so no event can be written without inventing the indication. The bipolar disorder half is coded as owen-1309-a.
RAMHT is the forecaster's own event (organizer, per affiliations; co-founded with Grady Hannah). Own-venture commitment with a date (2025-01-12), never scored. Also outside the five areas.
The forecaster's own Health Insurance Masterclass workshop (co-created with Kari Groff) on 2024-12-04. Own event, never scored. Also outside the five areas.
The forecaster's own Health Insurance Masterclass workshop (co-created with Kari Groff) on 2024-12-09. Own event, never scored. Also outside the five areas.
The forecaster's own newsletter article plan (GLP-1 data in addiction). Own content, never scored. Also outside the five areas.

'RCTs aren't going away any time soon' names no countable set, threshold or series, and 'any time soon' is not a deadline. The text is Ben Spielberg's guest essay, adopted only with 'I tend to agree'; even as the author's own claim, no event can be written. The second sentence ('can't be the solution that we rely on as gold standard') is normative.
Restated hedged view that GLP-1 medicines 'maybe, help with addiction': no drug-indication pair, trial, endpoint, regulator or threshold is named, and 'help with' is not an observable outcome.

'Hold promise as both safer and more effective treatments in subsequent evaluations': 'hold promise' is not an observable outcome; no study type, endpoint, comparator or threshold is named; 'subsequent evaluations' carries no deadline and names no trial, so the ClinicalTrials.gov table rule cannot apply. Writing a head-to-head trial_result event against naltrexone would invent the study design. A coder who reads it as a comparative trial_result would split it into safer (-a) and more effective (-b); this coder does not.
Reminder of the forecaster's own three events (RAMHT and two Health Insurance Masterclasses), already coded CONTROL as owen-1311, owen-1312 and owen-1313. Own events, never scored.

CMS staff motivation under possible mass government firings: no observable event, series or threshold on either side of the conditional ('if everyone is maybe getting fired'). Nothing can be written without inventing a measure.

Present-tense claim about CMS's current capability ('can't change the price of drugs in our current system'); no future state is asserted. The implied consequence of an attempt, a 'knock-down, drag-out fight' with pharmaceutical companies, has no observable criterion, so a coder who reads it as predictive would code VAGUE.

Normative imperative (create payment pathways for breakthrough devices) plus a consequence with no series, threshold or period: 'over the long term, you'll pay less' cannot be written as a quantity event without inventing the metric and the period. The condition (CMS creates the pathways) is outside the forecaster's control, but the consequent is not codable.

Consequence of hypothetical CMS device-payment pathways: 'won't have to pay off the big pharmacy benefit managers' has no series, threshold or observable event. Conditional on CMS action with no codable consequent.

Conditional consequences of device payment (devices reach patients 'rapidly'; investment 'into technology, not just pharma') with no series, threshold, period or countable set; 'would' is hypothetical. Compound, but neither half can be written.

'It's going to cost more' and 'drug prices go up forever': no named series, threshold, period or comparator, and the drug-centered strategy in the condition is not defined. 'Forever' is not a deadline.

'That will eat up your entire budget at CMS, given enough time': an open-ended horizon (not a deadline), no named series for PBM rebates or for the CMS budget, and the 8.8 percent growth figure is a premise, not a forecast with a period. Conditional on inaction ('If you let it').
'Better outcomes' from paying physicians more under at-risk contracts: no outcome measure, series, threshold or period. Conditional on CMS action that is not defined.
Imperative sentence (normative); the predictive clause 'will allow physicians in the outpatient setting to drive down costs' has no series, threshold, period or countable set.

Hedged, conditional pay-parity claim ('might mean you have to pay psychiatrists as much as neurosurgeons') with no named compensation series, period or criterion for the condition (outcome-based payment reform), which is itself undefined. The author flags self-interest ('Said a psychiatrist!').

A federal personnel recommendation and a judgment that Drew Pinsky would 'do a good job' as SAMHSA administrator: not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. The recommendation ('should be') is normative, and 'do a good job' has no criterion.
Whether Pinsky's vaccine stance is a 'dealbreaker' for Kennedy in a personnel choice: outside the five areas, and no observable event is named.
Public outrage at a hypothetical Pinsky appointment: outside the five areas; no countable set or threshold, and conditional on an appointment that is not the claim.
Pinsky's understanding of patient needs if appointed to lead SAMHSA: outside the five areas; no observable criterion.
Pinsky's acceptability to conservatives: outside the five areas; no observable criterion or countable set.
